title: Context and Evidence Construction
summary: This intermediate module teaches you to construct a focused context packet that connects each requested claim to relevant evidence. After completing it, you can organize retrieved passages, preserve source locations, and test whether an answer is supported by the supplied context.
objectives: Construct a context packet that separates the task, evidence, and response requirements.
Create evidence records that connect source passages to the claims they may support.
Order and label evidence so that important passages are easier to locate within a long context.
Audit a draft answer by tracing its claims back to evidence in the context packet.
Explain what changed in this source-correction update and which guidance the change affected.

sections.title: Level and scope
paragraphs: This is an intermediate-level module. It assumes that you can read a source, identify a passage relevant to a question, and write a basic instruction for a language model. It does not require knowledge of a particular provider, product, programming language, or retrieval system.

Context construction is the deliberate selection and organization of information supplied for a task. Evidence construction is the narrower process of recording which source passage supports which possible claim. A useful context packet keeps the task, the evidence, and the response requirements distinct.

sections.title: What changed in this update
paragraphs: The previous source entry, content/modules/ai-foundations/context-and-evidence-construction.json, had an unregistered publisher and had never been verified. It was a repository-relative path rather than a directly accessible HTTPS source, so it was removed from the source list.

The changed citation affected the module's support for two topics: using retrieved passages as external evidence and arranging evidence within long contexts. Those topics are now supported by the canonical records listed in the sources field. The correction is limited to source attribution and the explanations that depend on those sources. It does not add provider-specific tools, versions, or configuration.

sections.title: Separate the parts of a context packet
paragraphs: Begin with a task statement that identifies the requested output and its boundaries. Place source material in a separate evidence area, then state the response requirements separately. This structure helps prevent an instruction from being mistaken for evidence and prevents source text from silently changing the task.

For example, a task might request a short explanation of a policy. The evidence area would contain passages from the policy source, while the response requirements would say whether to cite source locations and what to do when the supplied evidence is insufficient. The task statement is not proof of the policy, and an output-format rule is not evidence for a factual claim.

sections.title: Build traceable evidence records
paragraphs: Represent each useful passage as an evidence record with four parts: a source label, an exact passage or faithful extract, a location that lets a reader find it again, and a short note describing the claim it may support. The support note is a proposed connection, not a substitute for reading the passage.

Keep qualification and limiting language with the passage. Removing words that express scope, conditions, or uncertainty can make the evidence appear to support a broader claim than the source provides. If no supplied passage supports a necessary claim, treat that claim as unsupported rather than filling the gap from assumption.

Research on retrieval-augmented generation describes combining generated text with retrieved external passages. This supports the practice of preserving retrieved evidence as a distinct part of the input instead of treating every requested fact as if it must come from internal model memory.

sections.title: Arrange evidence for use
paragraphs: Group evidence by the question or claim it addresses. Remove exact duplicates, retain passages that express meaningful disagreement, and give every retained item a stable label that can be referenced in the answer. Put the most directly relevant material close to the instruction that requires it, while preserving enough surrounding text to interpret the passage.

Experiments reported in Lost in the Middle found that performance could decline when relevant information appeared in the middle of a long input, even for models designed to accept long contexts. The reported performance was often better when the relevant information appeared near the beginning or end. This does not prove that one position is always best, but it supports testing evidence placement instead of assuming that every position in a long context will be used equally well.

sections.title: Audit the answer against the packet
paragraphs: After drafting, list the answer's checkable claims. For each claim, identify the evidence label and passage that supports it. A claim passes the audit when the cited passage supports the claim at the same level of scope and certainty. A citation that merely discusses the same topic is not sufficient.

Revise or remove claims that have no supporting passage. If passages conflict, report the conflict rather than selecting one silently. Also check that source labels in the answer point to the intended evidence records and that the recorded locations allow another reader to find the passages.

A completed packet therefore supports a repeatable workflow: define the task, collect traceable passages, connect passages to possible claims, arrange the evidence, draft the answer, and audit each checkable claim. After this module, you can perform that workflow instead of supplying an undifferentiated block of source text.
sections.callout: Evidence relevance and evidence sufficiency are different. A passage can be related to a claim without being strong enough to support that claim.

questions.prompt: Which context-packet structure does the module recommend?
choices: Combine the task, evidence, and response requirements into one unlabeled block.
Keep the task, evidence, and response requirements distinct.
Provide evidence only after the answer has been written.
Treat output-format rules as factual evidence.
questions.explanation: The module recommends separating the task statement, evidence area, and response requirements so that instructions are not mistaken for evidence.

questions.prompt: Which set contains all four parts of an evidence record described in the module?
choices: Source label, passage, retrievable location, and support note
Task statement, answer length, tone, and deadline
Source title, model preference, output style, and confidence score
Passage, final answer, hidden assumption, and formatting rule
questions.explanation: The module defines an evidence record as a source label, a passage or faithful extract, a location, and a note identifying the claim it may support.

questions.prompt: What conclusion does the module draw from the cited long-context research?
choices: Relevant information must always be placed in the exact center.
Every position in a long context is used equally well.
Evidence placement should be tested rather than assumed to have no effect.
Long contexts eliminate the need to label evidence.
questions.explanation: The cited experiments found position-related performance differences, so the module recommends testing placement rather than assuming equal use across the context.

questions.prompt: During the support audit, what should happen to a checkable claim that has no supporting passage?
choices: It should be retained without qualification.
It should be converted into an instruction.
It should be revised or removed.
It should be supported by an unrelated passage on the same topic.
questions.explanation: The audit procedure says to revise or remove claims that have no supporting passage.

questions.prompt: Why was the previous source entry removed in this update?
choices: It described a provider-specific procedure.
It was a repository-relative path from an unregistered publisher and had never been verified.
It used too many evidence records.
It reported a disagreement between sources.
questions.explanation: The update section states that the previous entry was an unverified repository-relative path from an unregistered publisher, not a directly accessible HTTPS source.
